```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Keutzer_2020_rifampicin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Keutzer_2020_rifampicin"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2020.00794> (open access)

Keutzer and Simonsson (2020) is a simulation study of model-informed
precision dosing (MIPD) for high-dose rifampicin. All of its simulations
use the Svensson 2018 HIGHRIF1 population PK model, which is already in
nlmixr2lib as `Svensson_2018_rifampicin` (one-compartment disposition,
Erlang transit absorption, Michaelis-Menten clearance scaled by an
auto-induced enzyme pool, dose-dependent bioavailability above 450 mg,
inter-individual variability on Vmax, km, V, ka, MTT and NN, and
inter-occasion variability (IOV) on km, ka, MTT and F).

To show what happens when IOV is ignored, the authors also re-estimated
that model on the original HIGHRIF1 data with all four IOV variances
fixed to zero. This "misspecified" model, with its re-estimated
structural, IIV and residual-error parameters (Table 4) and its full
NM-TRAN code (Supplementary Appendix S1), is the new model contributed by
this paper and is packaged here as `Keutzer_2020_rifampicin`. The
original model's estimates printed in the same Table 4 agree with
`Svensson_2018_rifampicin` to the printed precision (checked below), so
this vignette uses that model for the paper's IOV simulations.

# Population

The re-estimation used the HIGHRIF1 data set: 83 adults with
drug-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis from Cape Town, South Africa (59
male, 24 female), receiving 10 to 35 mg/kg rifampicin once daily. Body
weight was 55.1 kg on average (range 40.2-84.2 kg) and fat-free mass
40.0 kg (28.5-57.9 kg) (Keutzer 2020 Table 1). The same information is
recorded in `readModelDb("Keutzer_2020_rifampicin")` as the `population`
metadata.

# Source trace

| Element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `lvmax` | log(309.8) mg/h at FFM 70 kg | Table 4, Vmax (S1 THETA(1) 310) |
| `lkm` | log(15.8) mg/L | Table 4, km; S1 THETA(2) |
| `lvc` | log(93.6) L at FFM 70 kg | Table 4, V; S1 THETA(3) |
| `lka` | log(2.4) 1/h | Table 4, ka; S1 THETA(4) |
| `lmtt` | log(0.812) h | Table 4, MTT 0.81; S1 THETA(8) |
| `lnn` | log(7.568) | Table 4, NN 7.6; S1 THETA(9) |
| `emax` | 1.219 | Table 4, Emax 1.2; S1 THETA(5) |
| `ec50` | 0.05256 mg/L | Table 4, EC50 0.053; S1 THETA(6) |
| `kenz` | 0.005328 1/h | Table 4, kENZ 0.0053; S1 THETA(7) |
| `femax` | 0.401 | Table 4, Fmax 0.40; S1 THETA(10) |
| `fed50` | 17.35 mg | Table 4, ED50 17.4; S1 THETA(11) |
| `etalkm + etalvmax` | c(0.64996, 0.26529, 0.30515) | Table 4, IIV km 80.6%, IIV Vmax 55.2%, correlation 59.6% (variance = SD^2) |
| `etalvc` | 0.0074218 | Table 4, IIV V 8.6% |
| `etalmtt` | 0.34516 | Table 4, IIV MTT 58.8% |
| `etalnn` | 0.81866 | Table 4, IIV NN 90.5% |
| `etalka` | 0.082254 | Table 4, IIV ka 28.7% |
| `expSd` | 0.569 | Table 4, additive error on log scale 56.9% |
| Allometry | Vmax x (FFM/70)^0.75, V x (FFM/70) | S1 `$PK` ALLMCL, ALLMV |
| Bioavailability | 1 + Fmax (DOSE-450)/(ED50 + DOSE-450) | Eq. 3; S1 TVBIO |
| Absorption | Erlang transit input `transit(nn, mtt, bio)`, F1 = 0 | S1 `$PK` / `$DES` DADT(1) |
| Elimination | Vmax/(km + Cp) x A(2)/V x enzyme | Eq. 4; S1 `$DES` DADT(2) |
| Auto-induction | kENZ (1 + Emax Cp/(EC50 + Cp)) - kENZ enzyme | S1 `$DES` DADT(3) |
| Initial states | central 0.0001 mg, enzyme 1 | S1 `$PK` A_0(2), A_0(3) |
| Residual error | log-transformed DV, additive | Methods; S1 `$ERROR` |
| No IOV | all four IOV variances 0 FIX | Table 4; S1 `$OMEGA` |

## Original versus re-estimated estimates

Table 4 prints the original Svensson 2018 estimates next to the
re-estimated ones. The chunk below reads both packaged models and shows
that the original column is what `Svensson_2018_rifampicin` carries
(Table 4 percentages are SD x 100 for the random effects).

```{r table4}
# The occasion etas of the Svensson model are switched by OCC indicators
# and so are not mu-referenced; rxode2 notes this with a warning on every
# parse, which is expected for this model and is muffled here only.
quiet_parse <- function(expr) {
  withCallingHandlers(expr, warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("non-mu referenced", conditionMessage(w))) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  })
}
sv <- quiet_parse(rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Svensson_2018_rifampicin")))
ke <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Keutzer_2020_rifampicin"))
sv_ui <- sv
ke_ui <- ke

th <- function(ui) ui$theta
om <- function(ui) ui$omega

summ <- function(ui) {
  t <- th(ui)
  o <- om(ui)
  c(
    "Vmax (mg/h/70 kg)" = exp(t[["lvmax"]]),
    "km (mg/L)" = exp(t[["lkm"]]),
    "V (L/70 kg)" = exp(t[["lvc"]]),
    "ka (1/h)" = exp(t[["lka"]]),
    "MTT (h)" = exp(t[["lmtt"]]),
    "NN" = exp(t[["lnn"]]),
    "Emax" = t[["emax"]],
    "EC50 (mg/L)" = t[["ec50"]],
    "kENZ (1/h)" = t[["kenz"]],
    "Fmax" = t[["femax"]],
    "ED50 (mg)" = t[["fed50"]],
    "IIV Vmax (%)" = 100 * sqrt(o["etalvmax", "etalvmax"]),
    "IIV km (%)" = 100 * sqrt(o["etalkm", "etalkm"]),
    "IIV V (%)" = 100 * sqrt(o["etalvc", "etalvc"]),
    "IIV ka (%)" = 100 * sqrt(o["etalka", "etalka"]),
    "IIV MTT (%)" = 100 * sqrt(o["etalmtt", "etalmtt"]),
    "IIV NN (%)" = 100 * sqrt(o["etalnn", "etalnn"]),
    "Correlation Vmax-km (%)" = 100 * o["etalkm", "etalvmax"] /
      sqrt(o["etalkm", "etalkm"] * o["etalvmax", "etalvmax"])
  )
}

tab4 <- tibble::tibble(
  Parameter = names(summ(sv_ui)),
  table4_original = c(
    525, 35.3, 87.2, 1.77, 0.51, 23.8, 1.16, 0.0699, 0.00603, 0.504, 67.0,
    30.0, 35.8, 7.86, 33.8, 38.2, 77.9, 38.9
  ),
  packaged_svensson = unname(summ(sv_ui)),
  table4_no_iov = c(
    309.8, 15.8, 93.6, 2.4, 0.81, 7.6, 1.2, 0.053, 0.0053, 0.40, 17.4,
    55.2, 80.6, 8.6, 28.7, 58.8, 90.5, 59.6
  ),
  packaged_keutzer = unname(summ(ke_ui))
)

stopifnot(
  # Both packaged models reproduce their Table 4 column to rounding.
  all(abs(tab4$packaged_svensson / tab4$table4_original - 1) < 0.01),
  all(abs(tab4$packaged_keutzer / tab4$table4_no_iov - 1) < 0.02)
)

tab4 |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(
    -Parameter,
    ~ vapply(.x, function(v) format(signif(v, 4), scientific = FALSE, drop0trailing = TRUE), "")
  )) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Table 4, original" = table4_original,
    "Svensson_2018_rifampicin" = packaged_svensson,
    "Table 4, without IOV" = table4_no_iov,
    "Keutzer_2020_rifampicin" = packaged_keutzer
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Keutzer 2020 Table 4 against the two packaged models.")
```

# Virtual cohort

Following the paper's Methods, sex is drawn first (71.1% male), body
weight is then drawn from the sex-specific HIGHRIF1 distribution (mean
+/- SD 55.8 +/- 7.4 kg, range 40.7-74.0 kg for men; 53.8 +/- 10.7 kg,
range 40.2-84.2 kg for women; normal, truncated to the observed range),
and fat-free mass is derived with the paper's empirical relationships
(Eq. 1 for men, `FFM = 2.541 * WT^0.728`; Eq. 2 for women,
`FFM = 2.496 * WT^0.669`). Each dose group has 200 virtual patients.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(794)
n_per_arm <- 200
mgkg_groups <- c(10, 20, 25, 30, 35)

make_cohort <- function(n) {
  male <- stats::runif(n) < 0.711
  wt <- ifelse(
    male,
    pmin(pmax(stats::rnorm(n, 55.8, 7.4), 40.7), 74.0),
    pmin(pmax(stats::rnorm(n, 53.8, 10.7), 40.2), 84.2)
  )
  tibble::tibble(
    male = male,
    WT = wt,
    FFM = ifelse(male, 2.541 * wt^0.728, 2.496 * wt^0.669)
  )
}

cohort <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(mgkg_groups), function(i) {
  make_cohort(n_per_arm) |>
    dplyr::mutate(mgkg = mgkg_groups[i])
})) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    id = dplyr::row_number(),
    # Weight-band dosing: nearest 150 mg, never below the 450 mg reference.
    DOSE = pmax(450, round(mgkg * WT / 150) * 150)
  )

cohort |>
  dplyr::group_by(Sex = ifelse(male, "male", "female")) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    N = dplyr::n(),
    `WT mean (kg)` = mean(WT),
    `FFM mean (kg)` = mean(FFM),
    `FFM range (kg)` = paste(round(range(FFM), 1), collapse = "-")
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Simulated cohort (compare Keutzer 2020 Table 1).")
```

# Simulation

Daily oral dosing for 14 days with dense sampling over the 24-hour
dosing intervals of days 1, 7 and 14 (the paper's three sampling
occasions). `Svensson_2018_rifampicin` carries two IOV occasions
selected by `OCC`; days 1-6 and 14 are assigned occasion 1 and days 7-13
occasion 2, so each sampled day draws a fresh occasion effect relative
to its neighbour. Setting `OCC = 0` switches the IOV terms off, which
gives the paper's IIV-only simulation with the same individual (IIV)
parameters, because the solve is seeded identically. The Keutzer model
has no IOV, so `OCC` is not needed.

A maximum solver step of 0.02 h is used: with the short MTT and large NN
of some simulated subjects the transit input is a sub-hour pulse, and an
unconstrained first step after time 0 can step over it entirely.

```{r simulate}
obs_tad <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24)
sample_days <- c(1, 7, 14)

dose_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = cohort$id, day = 1:14) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = (day - 1) * 24, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot")
obs_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = cohort$id, day = sample_days, tad = obs_tad) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = (day - 1) * 24 + tad, evid = 0L, cmt = "central") |>
  dplyr::select(-tad)

events <- dplyr::bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(cohort, id, FFM, DOSE, mgkg), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    amt = ifelse(evid == 1L, DOSE, 0),
    OCC = ifelse(day >= 7 & day <= 13, 2L, 1L)
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, FFM, DOSE, OCC, mgkg)

solve_one <- function(model, ev, label) {
  rxode2::rxSetSeed(2020)
  quiet_parse(rxode2::rxSolve(model, ev, keep = c("mgkg"), returnType = "data.frame", hmax = 0.02)) |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, mgkg) |>
    dplyr::mutate(scenario = label)
}

sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  solve_one(sv, events, "Svensson 2018: IIV + IOV"),
  solve_one(sv, dplyr::mutate(events, OCC = 0L), "Svensson 2018: IIV only"),
  solve_one(ke, events, "Keutzer 2020: re-estimated without IOV")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    day = sample_days[findInterval(time, c(0, 6 * 24, 13 * 24))],
    tad = time - (day - 1) * 24
  )
```

# PKNCA: AUC0-24 on days 1, 7 and 14

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = paste0(mgkg, " mg/kg | ", scenario)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)

dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1L) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, mgkg) |>
  tidyr::crossing(scenario = unique(sim$scenario)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = paste0(mgkg, " mg/kg | ", scenario)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = (sample_days - 1) * 24,
  end = (sample_days - 1) * 24 + 24,
  auclast = TRUE,
  cmax = TRUE
)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id, concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h"),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id, doseu = "mg"),
  intervals = intervals
))

auc <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::mutate(day = sample_days[match(start, (sample_days - 1) * 24)]) |>
  tidyr::separate(treatment, c("dose_group", "scenario"), sep = " \\| ")
```

## Table 3: day-14 AUC0-24 with and without IOV

Keutzer 2020 Table 3 gives the median day-14 AUC0-24 of 1,000 simulated
patients per dose group from the original model, simulated with IIV only
and with IIV + IOV. The packaged Svensson model is compared against it
with `ncaComparisonTable()` (which compares medians).

```{r table3}
published_t3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~auclast,
  "10 mg/kg | Svensson 2018: IIV only", 39.9,
  "20 mg/kg | Svensson 2018: IIV only", 120.3,
  "25 mg/kg | Svensson 2018: IIV only", 151.4,
  "30 mg/kg | Svensson 2018: IIV only", 194.3,
  "35 mg/kg | Svensson 2018: IIV only", 248.7,
  "10 mg/kg | Svensson 2018: IIV + IOV", 39.3,
  "20 mg/kg | Svensson 2018: IIV + IOV", 123.5,
  "25 mg/kg | Svensson 2018: IIV + IOV", 155.3,
  "30 mg/kg | Svensson 2018: IIV + IOV", 202.6,
  "35 mg/kg | Svensson 2018: IIV + IOV", 261.9
)

day14 <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(start == 13 * 24, grepl("Svensson", treatment))

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = day14,
  reference = published_t3,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(auclast = "h*mg/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Day-14 median AUC0-24, simulated vs Keutzer 2020 Table 3. * differs by >20%.")
```

```{r table3-check}
t3_check <- auc |>
  dplyr::filter(day == 14, grepl("Svensson", scenario)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(dose_group, scenario) |>
  dplyr::summarise(sim = stats::median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = paste(dose_group, scenario, sep = " | ")) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(published_t3, by = "treatment") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * (sim / auclast - 1))

stopifnot(
  nrow(t3_check) == 10,
  # Doses 20-35 mg/kg: weight-band rounding has little leverage there.
  all(abs(t3_check$pct[!grepl("^10 ", t3_check$dose_group)]) < 15),
  # 10 mg/kg sits on the steep part of the bioavailability curve near the
  # 450 mg reference, where the unpublished weight bands matter most.
  all(abs(t3_check$pct[grepl("^10 ", t3_check$dose_group)]) < 35)
)
```

The 20-35 mg/kg medians agree closely. The 10 mg/kg group is the most
sensitive to how doses were banded by weight (bioavailability changes
fastest just above the 450 mg reference dose and the paper does not list
the HIGHRIF1 weight bands), so a larger difference is expected there.

## Figure 5: AUC0-24 by sampling day at 35 mg/kg

```{r fig5, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
auc35 <- auc |> dplyr::filter(dose_group == "35 mg/kg")

ggplot(auc35, aes(factor(day), PPORRES, fill = scenario)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    outlier.shape = NA,
    coef = Inf,
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    width = 0.7
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1000)) +
  labs(
    x = "Day",
    y = "AUC0-24 (h*mg/L)",
    fill = NULL,
    title = "35 mg/kg once daily, AUC0-24 by sampling day",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Keutzer 2020 (whiskers span the full range here)."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")

auc35 |>
  dplyr::group_by(scenario, day) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median = stats::median(PPORRES),
    p2.5 = stats::quantile(PPORRES, 0.025),
    p97.5 = stats::quantile(PPORRES, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "AUC0-24 (h*mg/L) at 35 mg/kg by scenario and day.")
```

Figure 5 of the paper shows median AUC0-24 of about 450, 290 and 250-260
h*mg/L on days 1, 7 and 14, falling with auto-induction; the
Svensson simulation reproduces this. The re-estimated model without IOV
gives a similar population median at every day: its larger IIV and
residual error absorb the variability that the original model assigns to
occasions. Because its km is much lower (15.8 vs 35.3 mg/L) and its
IIV on km much larger (80.6% vs 35.8%), it also produces a heavy upper
tail of patients whose elimination saturates at 35 mg/kg, which is
visible in the 97.5th percentile on days 7 and 14.

```{r fig5-check}
med35 <- auc35 |>
  dplyr::group_by(scenario, day) |>
  dplyr::summarise(med = stats::median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop")
ref_med <- med35$med[med35$scenario == "Svensson 2018: IIV + IOV"]
ke_med <- med35$med[med35$scenario == "Keutzer 2020: re-estimated without IOV"]
stopifnot(
  # Both models were fitted to the same data, so their population medians
  # should agree; a transcription error in the re-estimated values would
  # move the whole distribution.
  all(abs(ke_med / ref_med - 1) < 0.2)
)
```

## Figure 4: magnitude of IIV and IOV in AUC0-24 at 1,800 mg

The paper quantifies IIV as the spread of steady-state (day 24)
AUC0-24 among 1,000 patients given 1,800 mg with IIV only (95% PI
136.9-369.7 h*mg/L; SD of log AUC 25.4%), and IOV as the spread for the
typical patient over 1,000 occasions with IOV only (95% PI 122.2-331.2
h*mg/L; 25.8%). The covariates of these patients are not given. Both
runs here use the HIGHRIF1 mean fat-free mass of 40 kg, so the spread
reflects the random effects only, as in the paper; with the cohort's
fat-free-mass distribution added, the IIV-only spread widens to about
30%. For the IOV-only run the IIV variances of
`Svensson_2018_rifampicin` are set to a negligible 1e-12, and the sampled
day (day 25) is the second occasion.

```{r fig4}
n_fig4 <- 200
ss_day <- 25
fig4_events <- function(ffm, occ_last) {
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_along(ffm), day = 1:ss_day) |>
    dplyr::mutate(time = (day - 1) * 24, amt = 1800, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_along(ffm), tad = obs_tad) |>
    dplyr::mutate(day = ss_day, time = (ss_day - 1) * 24 + tad, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central") |>
    dplyr::select(-tad)
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      FFM = ffm[id],
      DOSE = 1800,
      OCC = ifelse(day == ss_day, occ_last, ifelse(occ_last == 0L, 0L, 1L))
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

iiv_ev <- fig4_events(rep(40, n_fig4), occ_last = 0L)
iov_ev <- fig4_events(rep(40, n_fig4), occ_last = 2L)

sv_iov_only <- quiet_parse(sv |>
  rxode2::ini(
    etalkm + etalvmax ~ c(1e-12, 0, 1e-12),
    etalvc ~ 1e-12,
    etalmtt ~ 1e-12,
    etalnn ~ 1e-12,
    etalka ~ 1e-12
  ))

auc_ss <- function(model, ev, label) {
  rxode2::rxSetSeed(2402)
  s <- quiet_parse(rxode2::rxSolve(model, ev, returnType = "data.frame", hmax = 0.02)) |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, Cc)
  conc <- s |> dplyr::mutate(treatment = label)
  dose <- ev |> dplyr::filter(evid == 1L) |> dplyr::select(id, time, amt) |>
    dplyr::mutate(treatment = label)
  res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id, concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h"),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id, doseu = "mg"),
    intervals = data.frame(start = (ss_day - 1) * 24, end = ss_day * 24, auclast = TRUE)
  ))
  as.data.frame(res$result) |> dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast")
}

fig4 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  auc_ss(sv, iiv_ev, "IIV only (200 patients)"),
  auc_ss(sv_iov_only, iov_ev, "IOV only (typical patient, 200 occasions)"),
  auc_ss(ke, iiv_ev, "Keutzer 2020 without IOV (200 patients)")
)

fig4_summary <- fig4 |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median = stats::median(PPORRES),
    p2.5 = stats::quantile(PPORRES, 0.025),
    p97.5 = stats::quantile(PPORRES, 0.975),
    sd_log_pct = 100 * stats::sd(log(PPORRES)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
fig4_summary |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    tibble::tribble(
      ~treatment, ~published,
      "IIV only (200 patients)", "136.9-369.7; 25.4%",
      "IOV only (typical patient, 200 occasions)", "122.2-331.2; 25.8%"
    ),
    by = "treatment"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Scenario" = treatment,
    "Median" = median,
    "2.5th pct" = p2.5,
    "97.5th pct" = p97.5,
    "SD of log AUC (%)" = sd_log_pct,
    "Published 95% PI; SD (%)" = published
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Steady-state AUC0-24 (h*mg/L) at 1,800 mg (compare Keutzer 2020 Figure 4).")

ggplot(fig4, aes(treatment, PPORRES)) +
  geom_boxplot(coef = Inf) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "AUC0-24 (h*mg/L)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Keutzer 2020 (whiskers span the full range here)."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1))

sd_iiv <- fig4_summary$sd_log_pct[fig4_summary$treatment == "IIV only (200 patients)"]
sd_iov <- fig4_summary$sd_log_pct[fig4_summary$treatment == "IOV only (typical patient, 200 occasions)"]
stopifnot(
  # Published 25.4% (IIV) and 25.8% (IOV); the Monte Carlo SE of an SD
  # from 200 draws is about 1.3 percentage points.
  abs(sd_iiv - 25.4) < 6,
  abs(sd_iov - 25.8) < 6
)
```

The packaged Svensson model reproduces the paper's finding that
variability between occasions in the same patient is as large as the
variability between patients. The re-estimated model without IOV, by
construction, puts all of that variability between patients and has a
wider IIV distribution of AUC0-24.

# Typical-value profiles

```{r typical, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
typ_ev <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(id == 1) |>
  dplyr::mutate(FFM = 40, DOSE = 1800, amt = ifelse(evid == 1L, 1800, 0))

typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  quiet_parse(rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(sv), typ_ev, returnType = "data.frame", hmax = 0.02)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(model = "Svensson_2018_rifampicin"),
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ke), typ_ev, returnType = "data.frame", hmax = 0.02) |>
    dplyr::mutate(model = "Keutzer_2020_rifampicin")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    day = sample_days[findInterval(time, c(0, 6 * 24, 13 * 24))],
    tad = time - (day - 1) * 24
  )

ggplot(typ, aes(tad, Cc, colour = model)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~day, labeller = label_both) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)",
    y = "Rifampicin (mg/L)",
    colour = NULL,
    title = "Typical patient (FFM 40 kg), 1,800 mg once daily"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Random-effect scale.** Table 4 reports IIV and the residual error as
  percentages; for the original model these equal 100 x sqrt(variance) of
  the published Svensson 2018 estimates, so the re-estimated values are
  read the same way (variance = (percentage/100)^2). Supplementary
  Appendix S1 prints the same numbers in `$OMEGA` and `$SIGMA`
  (0.8062, 0.5957, 0.5524, ...); there they are the standard deviations
  and the km-Vmax correlation rather than variances, since the off-diagonal
  0.5957 equals the 59.6% correlation of Table 4. Reading them as NONMEM
  variances would imply a correlation of 0.89 and a residual SD of 0.75,
  contradicting Table 4.
* **Parameter digits.** Where Appendix S1 `$THETA` gives more digits than
  Table 4 and rounds to the Table 4 value, the S1 digits are used. Vmax
  is taken from Table 4 (309.8), which is more precise than S1 (310).
* **Residual error.** The model was fitted to log-transformed
  concentrations with an additive error (SD 0.569); it is encoded as a
  log-normal error, `lnorm(expSd)`. Below-LLOQ handling (M3, LLOQ 0.13
  mg/L) is an estimation device and is not part of the model.
* **Bioavailability below 450 mg.** The published function has no lower
  bound and becomes unstable for doses just under 450 mg (its
  denominator crosses zero at 450 - ED50 = 432.6 mg). The paper fixed F
  to 1 at 450 mg because no lower doses were studied, so the packaged
  model clamps the excess dose `DOSE - 450` at zero. Doses of 450 mg or
  more, the range of the data, are unaffected.
* **IOV terms.** The re-estimated model fixes all four IOV variances at
  zero; they carry no information and are omitted rather than encoded as
  zero-variance etas, so the model needs no occasion column.
* **Simulation design.** The paper simulated 1,000 patients per dose
  group; 200 are used here. The HIGHRIF1 weight bands are not listed, so
  doses are mg/kg x WT rounded to the nearest 150 mg with a 450 mg
  floor. Weight is drawn from a normal distribution truncated to the
  sex-specific observed range rather than resampled from the individual
  HIGHRIF1 values, which are not published. The Figure 4 simulations
  assume a fat-free mass of 40 kg (the HIGHRIF1 mean) for every
  patient and occasion.
* **Not reproduced.** The MIPD results (Figures 6 and 7, bias and
  imprecision) require Bayesian estimation of individual parameters from
  sparse samples and a dose-selection algorithm, which are outside the
  scope of a model library vignette.
